outcome: Breast milk supply at 3 days and 1 month postpartum
Maternal salivary oxytocin levels at 3 days postpartum
cohort: 83 low-risk primiparous women who planned to breastfeed for at least 12 weeks postpartum
finding: Women who received epidural anesthesia during labor had lower breast milk supply in the early postpartum period and lower breastfeeding rates at 4 months postpartum, but intrapartum synthetic oxytocin use was not associated with breastfeeding outcomes.
mod_finding: Women who delivered using epidural anesthesia had lower breast milk supply in the early postpartum period and breastfeeding rates at 4 months postpartum compared to those who did not.
